question: A team lead is told by a colleague that "the client thinks the summaries are off". No example and no further detail came with it. What should she do first?
options: A) Get one specific summary the client objected to and what was wrong with it
B) Ask Claude to guess what a client in this sector would object to in a summary
C) Rewrite the shared instructions to make the summaries shorter and more formal
D) Stop using the arrangement until the client confirms the problem has been fixed
correct_answers: A) Get one specific summary the client objected to and what was wrong with it
explanations: Correct. Secondhand, unspecific feedback cannot be acted on. Getting one concrete example turns a rumour into something diagnosable, and it may turn out to be a single unusual case.
Asking Claude to speculate about the objection produces a plausible guess that is no closer to what the client actually said.
Changing shared instructions on a paraphrase risks fixing something the client never raised and breaking what already worked.
Suspending a working arrangement over an unexamined comment is a disproportionate response to feedback nobody has confirmed.
